fixed.problem: R-lock [minor]: no shared worktree lock. The merge step's git in a task folder (bringing main in, pushing it, moving the record to the pushed head) ran without the PR executor's lock, so a rebuild for a closed dependency could reset the branch mid-merge. The merge step then merged main into the rebuilt head, moved the voided record back to 'merging' (onNewHead) and merged it, so a dependent was merged without the person's look after its review was voided. Separately, when GitHub refused a held merge call because the rebuild pushed first, the merge step overwrote the rebuild's sentence with 'changed after the review'.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts 'a dependency closed while the person's Merge brings main into the dependent: the rebuild waits for the merge step's git, and the head that still holds the closed work is never merged (R-lock)' (failed: the rebuild force-pushed during the merge's git) and 'a dependency closed while the merge call is held open on GitHub: the rebuild pushes first, GitHub refuses the old head, and the record keeps the rebuild's word (R-lock)' (failed: the sentence was replaced). Follow-up 441ab43 also restores apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts's docs and take-out Merge cases. Those failed after 4e7e2dc because mergeAsIs has no stored record.
fixed.how: packages/capabilities/src/githost/worktree-lock.ts exports inWorktree (waits), tryWorktree (skips a busy folder) and worktreeBusy, keyed by the resolved path. pr-executor imports them. loop/merge.ts takes the lock for four things: (1) mergeChecked's update path, which re-reads the PR head inside the lock, then fetches, merges the base, pushes and calls onNewHead; (2) conflictsIn; (3) keepsOwnChange; (4) mergeReviewed's head read and lookFor's base comparison. A rebuild that finds the folder busy is owed (R-owed marks the record before any rebuild starts). run() does not claim a record with rebuild_owed_for set. Inside the call, onNewHead and a new stillMayMerge(head) hook run just before the record moves and just before host.mergePullRequest. Each returns false when the record is no longer 'merging' at the head this call holds, or when it owes a rebuild. The tool then returns superseded and run() puts the record back to 'queued', keeping its approval. After any call that did not merge, a record someone else moved keeps that word. GitHub merges only the sha the call names, so a rebuild pushed after the last check makes GitHub refuse. The checks apply only to run()'s stored records (call(..., fenced=true)). mergeAsIs (docs and take-out PRs) is unchanged.

fixed.problem: R-owed [minor]: rebuilds that could not run (a busy or dirty folder, a failed step) were remembered only in memory. A squash-merge or close seen while the dependent's folder was busy, followed by a restart, was never rebuilt, so the dependent's PR kept the dependency's commits and files.

fixed.how: Migration 0008 adds merge_record.rebuild_owed_for (nullable). MergeRecordRepo.oweRebuild(taskId, depId|null) keeps the first owed dependency; owedRebuilds(projectId) lists them. DependentBranches.rebuildFor marks every done dependent with a record before the rebuild starts (markOwed). It settles from the outcome: busy, held or failed stays owed; rebuilt or conflict clears it; unchanged clears only what was owed for this dependency. sweep() reads the owed records at every poll, including the first after a restart, and clears those whose task is no longer done. Tasks with no record keep the old in-memory fallback. ReviewedPrMerge.run reads its record fresh before claiming, because an owed mark bumps the version. data-model.md was regenerated.

fixed.how: DependentBranches.pullRequestState keeps the watcher's read of each open task PR for the poll. The watcher already reads every open PR each poll, so no GitHub call is added. sweep(), after the poll's rebuilds, drops PRs rebuilt in the poll and calls conflictNotice. It applies to a done task whose record waits for the person (left_to_you, or queued with approval none) and whose PR has mergeable === false. The record moves to left_to_you with last_outcome 'conflict' and conflictNoticeSentence(pr, base, files); the files come from the new PrTaskExecutor.conflictsWithBase. One left-open card is filed (change_card notice:'conflict', base; options REBUILD_CARD_OPTIONS.conflict = Redo / Leave it open); an already open merge card is patched instead. last_outcome dedupes across polls and restarts. A rebuild owed, or a rebuild_conflict, comes first. When mergeable is true again, the record goes to last_outcome 'conflict_resolved' with an empty sentence, Merge is offered again, and the open conflict card is withdrawn. The Overview row is blocked through the existing NO_CLICK. sweep returns true when it said or took back a notice. compose.ts (one hunk) then emits the project event. request-words.ts (one hunk) titles the card '"<task>" conflicts with main'. GitHostWatcherDeps.onDefaultBranchHead now returns unknown.

not_done.problem: A rebuild owed because the dependent's folder holds changes nobody committed blocks that PR's merge until the person clears the folder. If the person presses Merge, the record waits 'queued' (the row reads as merging) with no sentence saying why.
not_done.why: The fence is the safe direction: merging a branch that still holds a closed dependency's work is the worst outcome. A sentence for 'waits for its rebuild' is a new piece of wording (polish's), and what to tell the person about a dirty task folder (which they normally never touch) is a product choice. It happens only when someone edited a task's worktree by hand.

not_done.problem: A merge that GitHub completes before the watcher has even read the dependency's close can still carry the closed dependency's work.
not_done.why: Inherent: the app learns of the close only at the next poll, so this is the same as the close coming after the merge. Everything from the moment the app knows (marking the rebuild owed, checking again before GitHub's merge, GitHub's own refusal of a moved head) is covered. Recorded in ADR 0111's amendment point 2.

not_done.problem: On a shared state store (peers), an owed rebuild mark or a conflict notice is not restricted to this install's agent's records: an install without the task's worktree would see 'unchanged' and could clear a mark set by the install that has it.
not_done.why: Peers and teams are out of scope this round (NEXT-SESSION.md). Restricting by agent would need DependentBranches to know the install's agent ids (a compose change). Noted for the collaboration wave.

not_done.problem: A fetch failure of this computer's copy (GitHub not answering, a refused token) is not shown on the Files line.
not_done.why: By design: it is not a copy that stopped following (the next poll fetches again). It is written in ADR 0113's amendment. Saying a transient network failure on Files would be a new product decision.

not_done.problem: Bench walk of R-lock, R-chain, R-owed and the notification.
not_done.why: They need a held host call, a busy folder across a restart, or a CI check, which the bench cannot stage reliably. They are covered by composed tests against the fake GitHub (dependent-branches-merge.test.ts, dependent-branches-restart.test.ts) and the real-daemon case for the notification. The bench before/after walked the two person-visible ones the spec asked for: the conflict card and the Files line.
